text.p: Analysts have maintained or slightly upgraded their profit forecasts for ING Groep NV (ING) after the Dutch financial services group's nine month profits.
British and Dutch analysts raised earnings per share (EPS) estimates by between one and seven percent, mainly for the 1996 and 1997 fiscal years.
The upgrades were attributed to extra provisions, which pave the way for future profit growth, lower than forecast tax charges and a stronger than expected banking performance.
Analysts were also guided by a profit forecast from the group, which was widely considered to be too conservative.
ING on Thursday posted a net profit of 2.34 billion guilders for the first nine months of 1996, up 24 percent on the same period a year earlier and broadly in line with most estimates.
It also forecast a clear increase of between seven and 12 percent in EPS for the full year.
Net profit in 1996 is now seen at 3.09-3.23 billion guilders, or 4.30-4.45 guilders per share, up from the 1995 result of 2.65 billion guilders, or 3.84 cents per share.
For 1997, the forecasts are 3.42-3.76 billion guilders, or 4.50-4.80 cents per share, and for 1998, they are 3.74-4.19 billion guilders, or 5.00-5.29 cents.

Andrew Goodwin of UBS said he expected lower tax charges in 1997 and 1998, adding that the 275 million guilders provided for future costs in the nine month period gave them scope to report higher profits in future.
"It gives them a pretty solid base going forward," he said.
The provisions, 125 million of which came in the third quarter, mainly cover the cost of introducing the Euro currency and computer system changes related to the year 2000.
In a report, Paribas Capital Markets said EPS growth in 1996 had to be more than 12 percent as EPS grew 13 percent in the first nine months and ING expected an improved final quarter.
Lehman Brothers analyst Michael Lindsay raised his 1996, 1997 and 1998 estimates by between three and seven percent after ING said it expected clearly higher 1996 profits.
"That's a message that the second half is going to be better than they thought," he said.
When announcing its half-year results, the group warned that profit growth would slow in the second half.
He said the provisions restrained current year profit but allowed ING to produce steadily rising earnings.
IRIS analyst Bart van der Feen said the third-quarter provisions were higher than he expected.
Van de Feen, who raised his 1997 EPs estimate marginally, said ING now had a considerable base for profit growth as the provisions represented up to 10 percent of reported profit.
Of the provisions made this year, 200 million guilders is estimated to be for the euro currency and year 2000.
ING has estimated the total cost of the single currency at between 200 million and 300 million guilders.
Jacob Bosscha of Bank Labouchere said he raised his 1996 EPS estimate to 4.40 guilders from 4.31 previously.
He was surprised by the strength of banking profits, partly attributing it the purchase of Poland's Bank Slaski.
Other factors were higher interest margins and good results from trading LDC debt.
But Bosscha said the increase in life insurance earnings was low, while non-life was better than expected.
ABN AMRO analyst Jeff Meys said the nine-month result was slighter better than he expected because it included an extra 125 million guilders of provisions.
But he left unchanged his forecasts, which were on the high side of the range. "What was disappointing was that the life insurance side didn't do that well," he said.
-- Garry West, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000
